source: Checklists of what a goal is actually made of.
confidenceNote: Line-item presets are starting points chosen for plausibility, not cost surveys.
note: SPEC.md Section 13 asks the Dream Calculator to become the shared Goal Costing Engine 'with a template library', and makes the Wedding calc structurally identical to it. These templates carry LINE-ITEM LABELS ONLY and no amounts. Costs are wildly regional and inventing them would put a fake number in front of someone planning a real thing; the value here is the reminder that the marriage licence, the survey fee and the travel insurance exist at all. A line may be an object instead of a label when it is priced PER UNIT — { label, unitLabel, unitsPerGroup } — which still carries no amount: it says a wedding is catered per guest and that guests arrive a table at a time, not what a guest costs (D-263). A line may carry pays: true — rent a lodger pays, the rent a year at home saves — typed positive and counted negative (D-269). Six more checklists arrived with D-270: fertility treatment, a surgery, a legal matter, a funeral, a move, starting a business. Still no amounts, anywhere.

templates.label: Sabbatical

templates.label: A car
templates.blurb: Price on the windscreen, plus what it takes to drive it away.

templates.label: Take in a lodger
templates.blurb: A year of rent coming in, and what a room costs to let. The first block here that pays you.

templates.label: A year at home
templates.blurb: Living with family for a year: the rent you would not pay, against what you put in and what it costs to get around.
lineItems: What you pay toward the house, a year
Getting there and back, a year

templates.label: Fertility treatment
templates.blurb: Priced a cycle at a time, because that is how it is billed and how the decision gets made.

templates.label: A surgery
templates.blurb: The deductible is the famous number. The rest is what the bill is made of.
lineItems: Coinsurance, up to the out-of-pocket maximum

templates.label: A legal matter
templates.blurb: A retainer, then hours. The hours are the part nobody budgets for.

templates.label: A funeral
templates.blurb: Nobody prices this ahead of time, and then it has to be paid for in a week.

templates.label: A move
templates.blurb: The movers are the small part. The deposit, the overlap month and setting up are the rest.

templates.label: Starting a business
templates.blurb: What it costs to open the door, and three months of keeping it open before anyone walks through it.
